newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia detains 211 illegal workers in blitz.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia detains 211 illegal workers in blitz.

text.p: Malaysian police have detained 211 illegal foreign workers in the past five days in a crackdown on people without valid employment permits, a police spokesman and local newspapers said on Sunday.

Newspapers reported that 150 foreigners were caught in illegal worker settlements around the Ampang area in central Selangor state in the past five days. Another nine were arrested on Saturday in southern Malacca state.
A police spokesman for the Kajang area in Selangor told Reuters on Sunday that another 52 were detained in checks on factories and worker settlements in separate operations there on Saturday.
A senior police official told The Sunday Star that some of the foreign labourers were hiding in jungles and plantations to avoid arrest.

"They hide out and sleep in the nearby jungles and plantations and only come back to their settlements to change before going to work," Assistant Commissioner of Police Mokhtar Hassan was quoted as saying.

Malaysia officially began clamping down on illegal foreign workers on Saturday at the end of a January 31 extended deadline set by the government for about one million illegal workers to leave the country or face prosecution.
From February 1, the government will start enforcing amendments to the Immigration Act which provide harsher punishment including stiffer fines, jail sentences and whipping for certain offenders.
Authorities had earlier set a December 31, 1996, deadline to register and legalise illegal foreign workers in the country.
There are an estimated two million foreign workers in Malaysia, but only about 700,000 have registered. They are mostly from Indonesia, Bangladesh and India.
Booming Malaysia, with a population of about 21 million, is worried about social disorder and crime resulting from the presence of a large foreign-worker community.
Under the amended immigration act which come into force on Saturday, employers who hire illegal immigrants can be fined between 10,000 ringgit ($4,024) and 50,000 ringgit for each employee.

Employers with more than five such workers face a mandatory prison term of up to two years. Those found guilty of bringing in workers illegally and illegal workers who re-enter Malaysia after being deported could facing whipping. ($1 = 2.4850)
